statement: arc-06's enforcer-lang-rust crate source (Cargo.toml, src/lib.rs, src/rules/{mod,no_reexports,error_handling}.rs, fixtures) never landed on rust-build. commit 5763f80 ("feat(arc-06): enforcer-lang-rust crate") only touched TEST_PROOF_EXPECTATIONS.md, memory/streams/arc-06.ndjson, and proof/ artifacts — zero crates/enforcer-lang-rust/** files. The real source exists only in orphaned commit 6337b92 ("wip(arc-06): mid-pack checkpoint"), which is NOT an ancestor of rust-build HEAD (verified via git merge-base --is-ancestor). crates/ on HEAD 4bb883d has no enforcer-lang-rust directory at all.
why: The mission briefing for arc-07 named enforcer-lang-rust as the sibling exemplar to read before building enforcer-lang-ts. A worker trusting that briefing would waste time searching for files that do not exist on the branch, or worse, silently proceed without noticing the sibling never actually landed (a staging/commit-scope bug in arc-06's final commit, likely a git add that missed the crate directory after the mid-pack checkpoint).
howToApply: Any future lane briefed to read a sibling crate as an exemplar should verify with `git log --oneline -- crates/<sibling>` and `git merge-base --is-ancestor <checkpoint-sha> HEAD` before relying on it being present. If the sibling's source is missing from HEAD, do not attempt to fix it yourself (out of your own workpack's owns: scope) — proceed using the shared base crate (enforcer-validator) directly, note the gap in your started-mail, and let the orchestrator decide whether to re-open arc-06.

evidence.ref: commit 5763f80 stat shows only .md/ndjson/proof files; commit 6337b92 has the real crates/enforcer-lang-rust/** files but git merge-base --is-ancestor 6337b92 4bb883d fails

statement: rules/rules.json's `triggers` field is NOT a uniform literal-keyword hint across the catalog: for validator `typescript/source-scan` rows, `triggers` genuinely lists source-level keywords/punctuation (e.g. TS-6.1's ["any","as any"]); but for validator `generic-scanner` rows (the TS-6/7/8 slice arc-07 owns), `triggers` is a single-element array that just RESTATES THE RULE TITLE verbatim (e.g. TS-6.11's triggers == ["Map<string, domain> APIs are forbidden"], identical to its title). A rule-spec author who blindly used `triggers[0]` as the detection needle for generic-scanner rows would build a validator that greps source files for an English sentence and never fires on real code.
why: This is a data-quality trap baked into the authoritative catalog itself, not a code bug — it only surfaces when a worker actually inspects triggers vs title for the generic-scanner-validator subset and notices they are byte-identical, which is easy to miss if you write detection code from a summary table instead of reading the full JSON record.
howToApply: Before wiring any generic-scanner-validator rule's detection pattern from rules/rules.json, diff that row's `triggers` against its `title` — if they match, `triggers` is useless for this row and the detection pattern must be derived from the rule's `snippet`/semantics instead (as arc-07 did for all 48 TS-slice generic-scanner rows in crates/enforcer-lang-ts/src/rules/generic_scanner.rs). Rows owned by a literal-trigger validator family (e.g. typescript/source-scan, python's equivalent) do not have this problem and triggers can be used directly.

evidence.ref: rules/rules.json TS-6.11..TS-8.9 generic-scanner rows: triggers[0] == title for every one of the 48 TS-slice rows

statement: A shared comment-only-line guard (skip matching on lines that are pure `//`/`/* */` comments, to avoid a forbidden pattern merely being MENTIONED in a comment) silently defeats any rule whose violation IS a comment directive. TS-2.1 ("suppression comments are forbidden": //eslint-disable, //@ts-ignore, //@ts-expect-error, //@ts-nocheck) is exactly this case — every one of its violations is, by definition, a comment-only line, so applying the default guard made its fail fixture never fire (validator silently returned zero findings on a fixture that should trip it).
why: This is the mirror image of mem-arc-06-0002's double-dispatch gotcha: guarding by POSITION (comment vs code) is usually correct and was added specifically to avoid false positives from doc-comment examples, but a uniform guard applied without checking each rule's own semantics can create a false NEGATIVE instead. The bug did not surface as a compile error or an obviously wrong count — it surfaced as `did not fire on fail fixture`, i.e. a validator that looked plausible until the parity harness (enforcer-validator::run_fixture_parity) actually ran it.
howToApply: When adding a shared text-matching guard (comment-skip, string-literal-skip, etc.) to a data-driven rule-spec table, make the guard PER-RULE OPT-OUT-ABLE (arc-07 added a `comment_guard: bool` field to RuleSpec, defaulting true, set false only for TS-2.1) rather than hard-coded crate-wide. Before shipping a new rule spec, ask "is this rule's violation ITSELF the thing the guard would filter out?" — if yes, disable the guard for that one rule rather than special-casing the guard function.

evidence.ref: crates/enforcer-lang-ts/src/rules/spec.rs RuleSpec.comment_guard field; source_scan.rs TS-2.1 sets comment_guard:false; caught by run_fixture_parity DidNotFireOnFail before the comment_guard field was added
